From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@peihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: PEI Health Legal <legal@peihealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify hosting boundary and SCCs for MSA/DPA

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the call this morning. A couple of quick asks so our legal team can finish their review:

1) We need explicit language confirming that EU patient data for our EMEA customers will be stored and processed only in the EU-hosted VPC variant of your Private offering. If there are fallbacks (e.g., for DR), please call those out and the contractual conditions that trigger them.

2) Can you send your proposed DPA redline and an SCCs mapping that shows where each SCC clause maps to Redwood’s controls (kms/hsm, subprocessor list, deletion/retention)?

3) We have a narrow procurement window — PEI wants to finalize legal and procurement signoff by end of next week (June 18). If anything in the MSA/order form/price needs to change because of the hosting constraint, please flag immediately.

Appreciate a tight turnaround — copying our in-house counsel so they see the ask.

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Grant
Head of Legal Operations
PEI Health

Attachments: PEI_DPA_questions_20260611.pdf (list of clause-by-clause questions)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify hosting boundary and SCCs for MSA/DPA

Hi Olivia —

Thanks — got this and the attached questionnaire. Quick summary of what I’m sending you now:

- Attached: RDW_proposed_DPA_redline_20260611.docx (proposed edits to the MSA/DPA with explicit hosting clause), and SCCs_mapping_matrix_20260611.xlsx (mapping to controls and subprocessor responsibilities).
- Key points called out in redline:
  * Clause 2.1 (Data Residency): added "Customer Data originating from EEA-resident end users will be stored and processed only in Customer-designated EU-hosted Private deployment unless Customer provides prior written consent for cross-border processing."
  * DR/Failover: added a narrow fallback (Clause 2.3) that requires documented incident escalation, encrypted transport, and an 8-hour notice to customer ops before cross-border DR invocation.
  * KMS/HSM: we’re proposing the option for a customer-managed key (bring-your-own-key) in Exhibit B; internal KMS controls are documented in the SCCs matrix.

Ben / Laura — can you validate the fallback wording and confirm the SLA/notice mechanics are acceptable operationally? Ben, procurement will want any pricing delta for EU-only hosting and any surcharge for a customer-managed key called out on the order form.

Olivia — I’ll start an internal legal review now and expect to have a clean redline + SCCs mapping uploaded to the Drive and a DocuSign envelope prepped for review by EOD tomorrow (June 12). If PEI needs the redline sooner for procurement, we can move up.

Action items I’m going to do before tomorrow EOD:
- Upload DPA redline and SCCs mapping to shared drive (link below).
- Flag any order form price/surcharge for EU-only hosting.
- Get legal ops to track changes and prepare a short summary table of differences vs. our default hosted terms.

Marissa
Marissa Cole

- SCCs matrix maps encryption, key management, subprocessor oversight, deletion/retention, and audit log retention to specific Exhibit references.

2) Procurement to confirm whether the onboarding surcharge and uplift are acceptable; if yes, Laura/Ben will finalize the order form and return the DocuSign envelope for signature.
3) If PEI needs any additional audit evidence (SOC2 test date, encryption spec sheet), we can attach via the Drive.

If PEI wants to accelerate to meet June 18, we can run a 30-minute legal sync Thursday and aim for a final signoff Friday. Let me know preferred time windows.

Thanks — I’ll track comments in the drive and loop in our engineering delivery lead if they want a technical call on KMS specifics.
